newsitem.title: USA: USDA orders recovery of pork funds used to snoop.
newsitem.headline: USDA orders recovery of pork funds used to snoop.

text.p: The National Pork Board is under orders to recover any check-off funds that were improperly spent for reports on environmental, farm and similar groups, the Agriculture Department said Friday.
For several weeks, activist farm groups have contended the National Pork Producers Council used farmer check-off funds to investigate critics, including family farm organizations.

"Check-off funds, paid by family farmers, are being used to investigate the activities of organizations involving those same family farmers in efforts to enhance their farming future," Chuck Hassebrook of the Center for Rural Affairs said earlier this week.

In a statement, Lon Hatamiya, head of the Agricultural Marketing Service, said the agency had looked into complaints that NPPC had used check-off funds for one such report. No check-off funds were used for that report, the review concluded, but it revealed that several similar reports had been prepared in 1996 at NPPC's request and paid for with check-off funds.
Hatamiya said an undetermined number of reports had been funded with $51,300 in checkoff money.
The National Pork Board and AMS were reviewing those reports to see if the exceeded the boundaries set by the 1985 that created the pork check-off program, Hatamiya said.
NPPC received check-off money as a contractor under the National Pork Board.
"The board must recover any check-off funds used by NPPC to obtain information which is proven to exceed the scope of a project USDA approved or was ineligible for check-off funding," Hatamiya said.
Check-off funds can be spent only on projects in the general categories of promotion, research and consumer information and the projects must be approved in advance by USDA.
